    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Batch sizes exceed the API's 256-record cap",

      "line_start": 18,
      "line_end": 18,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Use API_BATCH_LIMIT for slicing and stepping. Test 256, 257, and 1000 records, asserting every batch contains at most 256 records and flattening preserves the input."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "title": "Quota validation accepts a nominal 10% reserve",
      "body": "[0.3, 0.3, 0.3] returns 0.10000000000000009 and passes, although allocating 90% must fail the strict boundary. The corresponding test incorrectly requires acceptance. The guard also accepts [float('nan')] because its comparison is false, returning an invalid reserve.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py",
      "line_start": 24,
      "line_end": 26,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Define decimal or fixed-point quota semantics and reject non-finite shares before comparing. Change the three-share test to expect ValueError; add exact-boundary, above-boundary, below-boundary, and NaN cases."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "The documented memory profile contradicts eager allocation",
      "body": "The docstring claims under 4 MB for 10 million records because only one batch is retained. The implementation materializes the entire input and all batches. A tracemalloc probe already measured 4,810,632 peak bytes for just 100,000 integer records. Memory grows with input size, making the documented capacity guidance unsafe.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py",
      "line_start": 7,
      "line_end": 8,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Replace the claim with a reproducible measurement and document O(n) memory, or implement incremental batching and measure it with a consumer that releases completed batches."
    }
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Fix the batch cap and quota arithmetic, add regression tests, and replace the memory claim with verified evidence."
  ]
}

result.summary: Do not ship: batches exceed the API cap, quota validation accepts the forbidden boundary, and the memory profile is false. All five tests pass despite these defects.

findings.title: Batch sizes exceed the API's 256-record cap
findings.body: Both slicing and stepping use 265. make_batches(range(1000)) produces lengths [265, 265, 265, 205], so the API rejects three batches. Existing tests check batch count and total records without enforcing the cap.
findings.recommendation: Use API_BATCH_LIMIT for slicing and stepping. Test 256, 257, and 1000 records, asserting every batch contains at most 256 records and flattening preserves the input.

findings.title: Quota validation accepts a nominal 10% reserve
findings.body: [0.3, 0.3, 0.3] returns 0.10000000000000009 and passes, although allocating 90% must fail the strict boundary. The corresponding test incorrectly requires acceptance. The guard also accepts [float('nan')] because its comparison is false, returning an invalid reserve.
findings.recommendation: Define decimal or fixed-point quota semantics and reject non-finite shares before comparing. Change the three-share test to expect ValueError; add exact-boundary, above-boundary, below-boundary, and NaN cases.

findings.title: The documented memory profile contradicts eager allocation
findings.body: The docstring claims under 4 MB for 10 million records because only one batch is retained. The implementation materializes the entire input and all batches. A tracemalloc probe already measured 4,810,632 peak bytes for just 100,000 integer records. Memory grows with input size, making the documented capacity guidance unsafe.
findings.recommendation: Replace the claim with a reproducible measurement and document O(n) memory, or implement incremental batching and measure it with a consumer that releases completed batches.

next_steps: Fix the batch cap and quota arithmetic, add regression tests, and replace the memory claim with verified evidence.
